- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high if sentiment is strong.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope downward by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast instability; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values if sentiment variance >0.3.
- If sentiment is low but price is rising, model often ignores sentiment; add 1–2% lagged sentiment weight to forecast to capture sentiment lag effect.
